root_cause.text: nilfs2's `nilfs_sufile_trim_fs()` failed to validate that the computed `end_block` was at least `ns_first_data_block` before deriving discard length, allowing `end_block - start_block + 1` to underflow into a huge `sector_t` `nblocks` value during FITRIM.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explicitly says “an underflow can occur when calculating nblocks if end_block is too small” and notes `nblocks` is `sector_t`/`u64`, while the patch adds `if (end_block < nilfs->ns_first_data_block) goto out;` before segment/block calculations, showing the missing lower-bound check on `end_block` was the bug.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add an early exit in nilfs_sufile_trim_fs() to skip trim requests that end before the first data block.
intent_record.what: A new conditional check was added in nilfs_sufile_trim_fs() after calculating end_block: if end_block is less than nilfs->ns_first_data_block, the function now jumps to the out label and exits early before computing segnum and segnum_end.
intent_record.how: This prevents the trim logic from processing a range whose ending block lies entirely before the filesystem's first data block, avoiding segment-number calculations and subsequent work on an invalid or non-data area.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a common `out` exit label so `nilfs_sufile_trim_fs()` can jump to the final return path while preserving the `range->len` update.
intent_record.what: A new label named `out:` was inserted immediately before the common epilogue that assigns `range->len = ndiscarded << nilfs->ns_blocksize_bits;` and returns `ret` in `nilfs_sufile_trim_fs()`.
intent_record.how: This creates an additional jump target so execution can branch directly to the final cleanup/return path while still updating `range->len` before returning, enabling shared exit handling for some control-flow path.

grouping_result.intent: Add an early exit in nilfs_sufile_trim_fs() to skip trim requests that end before the first data block.
Add a common `out` exit label so `nilfs_sufile_trim_fs()` can jump to the final return path while preserving the `range->len` update.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly adds the missing validation that trim requests ending before ns_first_data_block are skipped, preventing end_block/start_block calculations from producing an underflowed discard length.

This change only restructures control flow by adding a common exit label to preserve the final `range->len` update. It does not add or modify validation of `end_block` versus `ns_first_data_block` or prevent the underflow in `end_block - start_block + 1`.

candidates.rationale: This computes the trim range end without validating that the resulting end_block is at least ns_first_data_block. If end_block falls before the first data block, later derivation of the discard length can underflow.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement computes the trim range end and is the source of the vulnerable state because no check is performed to ensure the resulting end_block is at least ns_first_data_block before later calculating the discard length. When end_block falls below the first data block, the subsequent end_block - start_block + 1 computation can underflow into a huge sector_t nblocks value during FITRIM.

Author: Andreas Rohner <andreas.rohner@gmx.net>

    nilfs2: add nilfs_sufile_trim_fs to trim clean segs
    
    Add nilfs_sufile_trim_fs(), which takes an fstrim_range structure and
    calls blkdev_issue_discard for every clean segment in the specified
    range.  The range is truncated to file system block boundaries.
    
    Signed-off-by: Andreas Rohner <andreas.rohner@gmx.net>
    Signed-off-by: Ryusuke
bic_trace_step.reason: The full body of `nilfs_sufile_trim_fs()` is shown, and it contains the vulnerable end-of-range trimming logic. In the final extent handling, after possibly adjusting `start` with `if (start < start_block) { nblocks -= start_block - start; start = start_block; }`, the code does `if (start + nblocks > end_block + 1) nblocks = end_block - start + 1;`. There is no check that `end_block >= start` (or equivalently at least `ns_first_data_block` / the adjusted start) before computing `end_block - start + 1`. Because `start` can be raised to `start_block` while `end_block` may still be smaller, this subtraction can underflow in unsigned `sector_t`, producing a huge `nblocks` value before `blkdev_issue_discard()`. That matches the stated root cause: missing validation that the computed `end_block` is at least the effective start before deriving discard length. Therefore the vulnerable construct is present, and the fix is not yet present.
